A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the BALD framework and its three attack mechanisms. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite the changed title, organization, and robotics experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original driving experiments, attack ablations, defense tests, and robot action-sequence evaluations in Table 2, Tables 3–4, Figure 5, and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original driving results and reports VirtualHome experiments and additional defense evaluations in Tables 3, 5, and 8.

M1.justification: The core procedures remain: ICL-assisted word-trigger selection followed by fine-tuning, scenario generation with contrastive boundary examples, and dual-trigger RAG poisoning. The VirtualHome experiments instantiate these mechanisms with task-specific code prompts; they do not establish a distinct new attack component or optimization rule.

E1.justification: Robotics already appears in v1, but its constitution-violation and action-sequence tasks are replaced by household plan execution in VirtualHome, including kitchen-conditioned attack scenarios. This substantially changes the robotics task requirements and evaluation environment. HighwayEnv and nuScenes/CARLA coverage is retained; CARLA is not newly introduced.

E2.justification: BadChain joins the robotics comparison in v2 Table 3; v1 Appendix C compares original, benignly fine-tuned, and word-backdoored GPT-3.5 models. V2 also evaluates ONION and random-word augmentation, benign post-fine-tuning, and adversarial fine-tuning defenses. The driving comparator set in Table 2 is unchanged.

E3.justification: V1 evaluates 22 benign and 20 adversarial robotics tasks through action-sequence validity or refusal. V2 executes plans and measures SR, PSR, and malicious goal completion, using ten reference tasks and a separate 19-task set for BALD-scene (Appendix A.3). New defense experiments introduce removal-depth and fine-tuning controls. NuScenes preprocessing is also described as using the first few frames instead of the first frame; this reported change does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds ONION sensitivity and efficiency analysis, training-stage defense tests, and simulator/reasoning case studies (Table 5, Appendix B, Figure 6, and Appendix C). V1's BALD-scene defense analysis varying benign ICL examples, Table 4, is removed. The existing component ablation and contrast-ratio, poisoning-ratio, and RAG-demonstration analyses remain as v2 Table 4 and Figure 7.

E5.justification: V2 Table 3 newly reports three runs and plus/minus values for robotics SR and PSR; v1's robotics results report counts without uncertainty. The dispersion statistic and seeds are unspecified, and this does not establish increased repetitions for the retained driving experiments.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in driving Table 2 are identical, and the existing component-ablation and Figure 5/7 results are retained. V1's robotics counts are replaced by different-setting VirtualHome results, including ASR of 20% for BadChain, 100% for BALD-word/RAG, and 85% for BALD-scene. New defense results include BALD-word ASR of 24% with ten ONION removals, 58% after benign post-fine-tuning, and 0% after adversarial fine-tuning. V1 Table 4's ICL-defense results disappear.

T1.justification: The threat-model assumptions change substantially: v1 Section 2.1 grants access to a subset of fine-tuning data for limited poisoning, whereas v2 Section 3.1 grants control over model fine-tuning and publication, permitting high poisoning rates subject to benign-performance constraints. This changes assumed attacker capabilities. Objectives O.1–O.3 remain mathematically unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a three-mechanism framework demonstrating effective, stealthy backdoors. V2 makes end-to-end embodied consequences and resilience against multiple defenses explicit headline contributions and adds quantitative success-rate summaries to the abstract. Embodied-agent terminology mostly sharpens an existing autonomous-driving/robotics focus.

C2.justification: V2 interprets scenario attacks as reversing alignment, explicitly excludes sophisticated white-box retrieval optimization, and distinguishes defenses according to knowledge of the trigger. Appendix A.3 newly explains why BALD-scene robotics scores are not directly comparable with other methods. These additions materially expand mechanism explanations, defense qualifications, and applicability boundaries; the earlier small-dataset limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds VirtualHome action/object interfaces, worked code prompts, goal-state construction instructions, and attack-specific GPT fine-tuning settings, plus implementation descriptions for the new defenses. It explicitly states that backdoored models are not released. Driving hyperparameters remain unchanged, while the earlier robotics generation recipe and explicit 124-example HighwayEnv evaluation count are removed.

R1.justification: The literature discussion is substantially refocused on embodied closed-loop agents. V2 adds positioning against Watch Out for Your Agents!, introduces ONION and VirtualHome-related literature, and removes the robot-constitution discussion and several broader backdoor references. Relocating related work and updating existing works' publication metadata are separate presentation changes.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and threat-model narrative, moves and revises related work into Section 2, and adds explicit takeaway statements throughout the research questions. Appendices A–C are reorganized around dataset evaluation, defenses, and reasoning examples, and an ethics subsection is added.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the overview and simplifies the scenario-generation diagram, adds a model-publication diagram and VirtualHome execution/environment figures, and removes v1's robot-constitution illustration. Robotics and defense tables are added or replaced, existing tables are relocated and restyled with shaded rows, and typography and page layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: Executing robot plans in VirtualHome and evaluating ONION and training-stage defenses provide stronger evidence of practical impact and mitigation than v1's action-sequence checks and ICL-only defenses. Three-run reporting and explicit evaluation caveats improve transparency. The gain is limited by small robotics test sets and the different test set used for BALD-scene: its higher SR/PSR cannot establish superior benign performance over the other methods. Headline success-rate summaries also need clearer qualification concerning aggregation and retrieval conditioning.
